2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the predecessor of opposite party, Salema Khatun as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No. 105 of 1989 subsequently, renumbered as Other Suit No. 41 of 1991 against the present petitioner and pro forma opposite party No. 11 as defendant for declaration of title by way of gift and adverse possession stating that the property in question belonged to one Nawab Ali, husband of the plaintiff who by a deed of gift dated 6-7-1969 gifted the suit land to the plaintiff and by other registered deeds of gift said Nawab Ali gifted his other landed property to his other heirs. Nawab Ali had four wives, the plaintiff is the second wife. Nawab Ali gifted some non-suited property to his son defendant No. 8, Md Muslim, but in the said deed of gift the deed writer wrongly included the suit property already gifted to the plaintiff. After making the gift by Nawab Ali in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff got delivery of possession, but for long time the plaintiff had no knowledge about inclusion of her gifted property in the deed of gift made by Nawab Ali in favour of his minor son Md Muslim. In fact the suit property never gifted to defendant No. 8, Muslim and Nawab Ali never expressed his willingness to make gift of the suit property in favour of Md Muslim. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 and 5-7 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the suit is barred by limitation and it has no cause of action. It was also alleged that the suit has not been filed by the plaintiff but it is filed by putting thumb impression of her son Mahbub. The suit property was gifted by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim by deed of gift No. 4073 dated 6-7-1969 and delivered possession of the same to him. The said Md Muslim while in possession and enjoyment of the suit property sold the same to the defendant, Abdul Jabbar, predecessor of the petitioners by a registered deed dated 15-12-1985 and delivered possession of the same. After purchase the said Abdul Jabbar got his name mutated in the khatian and have been in possession by giving boundary wall and barb wire fencing, the story of inclusion of the property in the deed of the plaintiff is false, baseless and fraudulently created for filing of this suit. 

 7. Mr Kamal ul Alam, Senior Advocate with Mr Md Masud Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submit that admittedly, the suit land belonged to Nawab Ali. The said Nawab Ali on the same date executed and registered two deeds of gift, one in favour of the plaintiff as his second wife and another in favour of his son Md Muslim, a son by another wife. In the schedule of both the deeds of gift the suit property covered by RS plot No. 172 measuring 21 sataks have been included. Subsequently, Md Muslim by a sale deed dated 15-12-185 sold 91 /2 sataks land to Abdul Jabbar, the predecessor of the present petitioners and delivered possession of the same to him. He further submits that while Abdul Jabber was in possession of the suit land all of a sudden the predecessor of the present opposite party, Salema Khatun claiming the property to be her gifted property instituted the instant suit for declaration of title by way of gift and adverse possession. 

 12. Admittedly, the suit property in question belonged to Nawab Ali who purchased the same from one Abdul Hoque by a register deed dated 27-1-1964. Said Nawab Ali executed two deeds of gift dated 7-6-1969 and registered on 8-7-1969 bearing Nos. 4073 and 4080 in favour of his son, Md Muslim and his second wife Salema Khatun respectively. 

 13. The deed of gift bearing No. 4073 was made by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim in respect of suit property along with other non-suited property. Deed of gift No. 4080 in favour of plaintiff, Salema Khatun was for suit property only. The suit property covered by RS plot No. 172 measuring 47 sataks land in total. As per plaint case 26 sataks of land was acquired by the government from Abdul Hoque. Nawab Ali purchased remaining 21 sataks of land from Abdul Hoque and the same was gifted by the aforesaid two deeds of gift in favour of wife of Nawab Ali and his son Md Muslim. Now the question has arisen, between the two deeds of gift for the same property which one shall prevail. The trial court in its judgment considered both the deeds of gift and considering evidences adduced by the plaintiff and the provisions of law held that: 

 14. From the above observations of the trial court it appears that the trial court considering all the evidences and circumstances held that the deed of gift made by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim is earlier one and as per section 47 of the Registration Act the deed of gift (exhibit-A) in favour of Md Muslim was executed earlier and shall prevail over the deed of gift executed in favour of plaintiff, Salema Khatun.
